items.pronunciation_notes: One long syllable with a soft final d: baad.

learn.explanation_en: बाद means after, and it works as part of the compound postposition के बाद: खाने के बाद, after eating. Note that the thing before it goes oblique — खाना becomes खाने — exactly as Module 6 taught for any noun in front of a postposition. बाद में on its own means afterwards or later, with no reference point named. The word is masculine, though you will rarely need that fact since it almost never takes an adjective.

examples.note: खाना goes oblique to खाने before के, since it is Class 1.
बाद में on its own means afterwards, with nothing named.
मिलना in the plural future, agreeing with an unstated हम.

common_error.why_en: खाना ends in -ा, so it is Class 1 and must go oblique before a postposition.

practice.question: बाद
practice.explanation_en: बाद means after, and it appears in the compound postposition के बाद.

game.explanation_en: के बाद. Its opposite पहले takes से instead, which is worth keeping straight.

items.pronunciation_notes: The middle vowel drops in speech, giving pah-le rather than pa-ha-le.

learn.title_en: से पहले — before, and the postposition is different
learn.explanation_en: This is the trap of the level. बाद takes के and पहले takes से: खाने के बाद, after eating, but खाने से पहले, before eating. The two are exact opposites and they do not share a postposition, so copying one across is the natural mistake. पहले on its own means earlier or first — पहले तुम बोलो, you speak first — and दो साल पहले means two years ago, with the time period simply placed in front.

examples.note: से rather than के, unlike बाद.
The period goes in front and no postposition is needed at all.
पहले on its own, meaning first in sequence.

common_error.why_en: पहले takes से. Copying के across from बाद is the commonest mistake with this pair.

practice.question: पहले
practice.explanation_en: पहले means before or earlier, and it also means first in a sequence.

game.explanation_en: से पहले — while its opposite बाद takes के. The pair does not match.

items.pronunciation_notes: The final ट is retroflex, as in every English loanword: mi-naṭ.

learn.title_en: एक मिनट is a phrase, not a measurement
learn.explanation_en: मिनट is borrowed from English, masculine and Class 2 so the plural is identical — दो मिनट, not दो मिनटें. The phrase worth having whole is एक मिनट, which functions like just a moment or hold on and rarely means sixty seconds. मिनट में means in a minute. Compare it with पल, which is a moment in the poetic sense and belongs to a different register entirely.

examples.note: A set phrase, used to ask someone to wait.
Class 2, so the plural looks identical to the singular.
लगना for time taken, in the plural future.

common_error.why_en: मिनट is masculine and Class 2, so the plural is identical. -ें is a feminine ending.

practice.question: मिनट
practice.explanation_en: मिनट is a minute, masculine, and unchanged in the plural.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with मिनट for time taken?
game.explanation_en: पाँच मिनट लगेंगे — लगना is the verb for time something takes.

summary.recap_en: बाद takes के and पहले takes से, which is the one thing to get right about this pair since they are opposites and do not match. Both put the noun in front of them into the oblique, exactly as Module 6 taught.
summary.next_up_en: Next: next, last, and age — three more things Hindi handles differently from English.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ग्ल cluster runs together with no vowel between: ag-laa.

learn.title_en: अगले हफ़्ते — the oblique doing adverbial work
learn.explanation_en: अगला is next, a marked adjective, so it agrees: अगला, अगली, अगले. The thing worth noticing is the time phrase. अगले हफ़्ते means next week, and both words are in the oblique even though there is no postposition visible. Hindi uses the oblique on its own to make a time expression adverbial — the same happens in पिछले साल and इस बार. So if a time phrase looks oblique for no reason, that is the reason.

examples.note: Both words oblique, with no postposition — this is how time phrases work.
Direct form, since this is not a time expression.
बार is feminine, so the adjective takes -ी.

common_error.why_en: As a time expression the phrase goes oblique, even with no postposition following it.

practice.question: अगला
practice.explanation_en: अगला is next, and it agrees with the noun it describes.

game.explanation_en: अगले हफ़्ते — time expressions take the oblique with no postposition.

items.pronunciation_notes: Aspirated chh in the middle and the cluster runs together: pichh-laa.

learn.title_en: पिछले साल — the same oblique trick
learn.explanation_en: पिछला is last or previous, the opposite of अगला, and it behaves identically: marked, agreeing, and going oblique in time expressions. पिछले साल is last year and पिछले हफ़्ते is last week, both with no postposition in sight. Note that Hindi does not use कल for last week or next week the way English uses yesterday and tomorrow loosely — कल is strictly the adjacent day in either direction, and anything further needs पिछला or अगला.

examples.note: Oblique with no postposition, as time expressions are.
बार is feminine, so the adjective takes -ी.
Direct form here, since this is not a time phrase.

common_error.why_en: In a time expression the phrase goes oblique. पिछला साल would be the last year as a thing being described rather than when something happened.

practice.question: पिछला
practice.explanation_en: पिछला is last or previous, and it is the opposite of अगला.

game.explanation_en: बार is feminine, so the adjective takes -ी and stays -ी in the oblique.

items.pronunciation_notes: The म्र cluster ends the word with no vowel after it: umr, one syllable.

learn.title_en: Age is something you have, not something you are
learn.explanation_en: उम्र is age, feminine and flagged. English says I am thirty; Hindi says मेरी उम्र तीस साल है, my age is thirty years — the age is a possession rather than a property of you. The question is तुम्हारी उम्र कितनी है, and the possessive is feminine because it agrees with उम्र. There is also a colloquial version using को: उसे कितने साल हुए. Both work, and the possessive one is more common.

examples.note: Both तुम्हारी and कितनी are feminine, agreeing with उम्र.
Literally my age is thirty years.
बढ़ना is intransitive, and रही agrees with उम्र.

common_error.why_en: That says you are thirty years, as an object. Age in Hindi is possessed rather than being what you are.

practice.question: उम्र
practice.explanation_en: उम्र is age, feminine, and it is expressed as something you have.

game.question_en: How do you ask someone's age?
game.explanation_en: तुम्हारी उम्र कितनी है — the possessive, feminine because it agrees with उम्र.

summary.recap_en: The time block is complete at twelve words. Time expressions take the oblique with no postposition — अगले हफ़्ते, पिछले साल — which explains a great many phrases that otherwise look wrong. Age is possessed rather than being what you are.
summary.next_up_en: Next: adverbs of manner, and the one pattern that generates most of them.

items.pronunciation_notes: Breathy dh at the front and a clear e at the end: dhii-re.

learn.title_en: धीरे covers slowly and quietly at once
learn.explanation_en: धीरे means slowly, and also gently and quietly — the common thread is reduced intensity, so धीरे बोलो can mean speak slowly or lower your voice depending on the situation. It never changes. The doubled form धीरे-धीरे means gradually or bit by bit, and it is one of the most used phrases in the language. Doubling has now appeared three times — बार-बार, कभी-कभी and here — and it consistently either intensifies or softens.

examples.note: Or speak slowly, depending on context.
The doubled form, softening rather than intensifying.
चलाना is transitive, so this is the imperative.

common_error.why_en: धीरे is an adverb and has one form. There is a related adjective धीमा, but धीरे itself never takes -ा.

practice.question: धीरे
practice.explanation_en: धीरे is slowly, and also gently or quietly — the thread is reduced intensity.

game.question_en: What does the doubled form धीरे-धीरे mean?
game.explanation_en: धीरे-धीरे means gradually or bit by bit. Doubling softens here rather than intensifying.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ध्य is a single cluster with the y folded in: dhyaan.

learn.title_en: ध्यान से — noun plus से makes an adverb
learn.explanation_en: ध्यान is attention, and ध्यान से means carefully or attentively. That is the pattern this whole block turns on: a noun plus से gives you an adverb of manner. You have already met आराम से for calmly, प्यार से for kindly and जल्दी से for quickly, and now ध्यान से and ज़ोर से join them. It is fully productive, so you can build adverbs from nouns nobody has taught you. ध्यान देना is to pay attention, and the thing attended to takes पर.

examples.note: Noun plus से, giving an adverb of manner.
देना for giving attention, in the तुम imperative.
The thing attended to takes पर, like भरोसा.

common_error.why_en: करना is the default guess again. Attention is given rather than done — though ध्यान करना does exist and means to meditate.

practice.question: ध्यान से
practice.explanation_en: ध्यान से is carefully or attentively — the noun ध्यान plus से.

game.question_en: Which postposition turns a noun into an adverb of manner?
game.explanation_en: से — as in ध्यान से, आराम से, प्यार से and जल्दी से.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted ज़ is a z and the vowel is a long open o: zor.

learn.title_en: ज़ोर से — the opposite of धीरे
learn.explanation_en: ज़ोर is force or strength, and ज़ोर से means loudly, hard or forcefully — the direct opposite of धीरे. Built with the same noun-plus-से pattern. You met ज़ोर already without knowing it: कमज़ोर, weak, is कम plus ज़ोर, less force. That kind of transparency is worth looking for, because a great many Hindi words are compounds of pieces you already have.

examples.note: The opposite instruction to धीरे बोलो.
The same pattern with another verb.
कम plus ज़ोर — less force — which is where the word comes from.

common_error.why_en: The से is what makes it an adverb. Without it you have just named the noun force.

practice.question: ज़ोर से
practice.explanation_en: ज़ोर से is loudly or forcefully — the opposite of धीरे.

game.question_en: Which word is built from कम plus ज़ोर?
game.explanation_en: कमज़ोर — less force, meaning weak. Many Hindi words are transparent compounds like this.

summary.recap_en: A noun plus से gives an adverb of manner, and the pattern is fully productive — ध्यान से, ज़ोर से, आराम से, प्यार से, जल्दी से. That single rule generates most of the manner adverbs in the language, so it is worth more than any individual word in this level.
summary.next_up_en: Next: how often things happen, and the adverb that goes with a guess.

items.pronunciation_notes: The क्स cluster runs together with no vowel between: ak-sar.

learn.title_en: अक्सर is the third habitual trigger
learn.explanation_en: अक्सर means often or usually, and like रोज़ and हमेशा it can only sit with the habitual — something that happens often cannot be described with the continuous. वह अक्सर देर से आता है. That gives you three reliable adverbs for choosing a tense, and between them they cover most cases where you are unsure. अक्सर never changes and it usually sits just before the verb, though it can move to the front for emphasis.

examples.note: अक्सर forces the habitual, as रोज़ and हमेशा do.

examples.hindi: मैं अक्सर देर से उठता हूँ
examples.read_as: maiṁ aksar der se uṭhtaa huuṁ
examples.note: देर से for late, and उठना is intransitive.
ऐसा means like this or such, and it agrees as a marked adjective.

common_error.why_en: The continuous describes one stretch of time in progress, which cannot be something that happens often.

practice.question: अक्सर
practice.explanation_en: अक्सर is often or usually, and it forces the habitual.

game.explanation_en: The habitual — joining रोज़ and हमेशा as a reliable tense test.

tts_strings: मैं अक्सर देर से उठता हूँ

items.pronunciation_notes: Breathy bh in the middle and a long ii at the end: ka-bhii.
items.gloss_en: ever, at any time; sometimes when doubled

learn.title_en: कभी नहीं for never, कभी-कभी for sometimes
learn.explanation_en: कभी on its own means ever or at any time, and it takes its real meaning from what surrounds it. With नहीं it becomes never: मैं कभी नहीं जाता. Doubled it becomes sometimes: कभी-कभी. And in a question it means ever — क्या तुम कभी गए हो. Hindi has no single word for never, so कभी नहीं is how it is built, and that is worth knowing because reaching for one word will leave you stuck.

examples.note: कभी plus नहीं is how Hindi says never.
The doubled form, softening as धीरे-धीरे does.
In an invitation it means at some point, unspecified.

common_error.why_en: कभी comes before नहीं, and the pair stays together in front of the verb.

practice.question: कभी-कभी
practice.explanation_en: The doubled form means sometimes. On its own कभी means ever.

game.explanation_en: कभी नहीं. There is no single word for never, so it is built from two.

items.pronunciation_notes: The length falls on the first syllable: shaa-yad.

learn.explanation_en: शायद means perhaps, and it pairs naturally with the presumptive forms from Module 7 — शायद वह घर पर होगा, he is probably at home. That is not a rule so much as a fit: होगा already carries the sense of a guess, and शायद makes it explicit. It also works with the future and with the plain present, and it always sits at the front of the clause rather than next to the verb.

examples.note: शायद with the presumptive होगा, which already means probably.
होगी agrees with the feminine बारिश.
With the plain present it softens a claim rather than guessing.

common_error.wrong: वह शायद घर पर है शायद
common_error.why_en: शायद sits once, at the front of the clause. It does not attach to the verb like other adverbs.

practice.question: शायद
practice.explanation_en: शायद is perhaps or maybe, and it sits at the front of the clause.

game.question_en: Which verb form pairs most naturally with शायद?
game.explanation_en: होगा — the presumptive, which already carries the sense of a guess.

summary.recap_en: अक्सर joins रोज़ and हमेशा as an adverb that forces the habitual, giving three reliable tense tests. Hindi has no single word for never — कभी नहीं builds it from two — and शायद pairs with the presumptive because both are about guessing.
summary.next_up_en: Next: absolutely and only, and a conversation about how often you come here.

items.pronunciation_notes: The doubled ल is held slightly and no vowel follows the final ल: bil-kul.

learn.explanation_en: बिल्कुल means absolutely or completely, and it strengthens whatever follows. On its own as an answer it means absolutely, yes. With नहीं it becomes not at all, which is far stronger than a plain नहीं — बिल्कुल नहीं is a flat refusal. It also means exactly: बिल्कुल सही, exactly right. Like every adverb in this block it never changes, and it sits directly in front of the word it is strengthening.

examples.note: Much stronger than a plain नहीं.
Here it means precisely rather than completely.
Strengthening the पता होना construction from level forty-one.

common_error.why_en: बिल्कुल is an adverb with one form. It never takes an ending of any kind.

practice.question: बिल्कुल
practice.explanation_en: बिल्कुल is absolutely or completely, and it strengthens whatever follows.

game.explanation_en: बिल्कुल नहीं is a flat refusal, much stronger than नहीं on its own.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted फ़ is an f and no vowel follows it: sirf, one syllable.

learn.title_en: सिर्फ़ goes directly in front of what it limits
learn.explanation_en: सिर्फ़ means only, and its position decides the meaning exactly as in English. सिर्फ़ मैं गया says only I went, nobody else; मैं सिर्फ़ वहाँ गया says I only went there and did nothing more. So it must sit immediately in front of the word it is limiting rather than drifting to the front of the clause. The Hindi word केवल means the same and is more formal, common in writing.

examples.note: Directly in front of what it limits.
Limiting तुम, so nobody else knows.
Limiting हिंदी — no other language, rather than no other activity.

common_error.why_en: The first says only I speak Hindi and nobody else does. Position decides what is being limited, as it does in English.

practice.question: सिर्फ़
practice.explanation_en: सिर्फ़ is only or just, and its position decides what it limits.

options: at the front of the clause
options_read_as: at the front of the clause
game.explanation_en: Directly before what it limits — exactly as only does in English.

items.pronunciation_notes: The doubled word runs together as one unit: ka-bhii-ka-bhii.

learn.title_en: Frequency adverbs, and the tense they force
learn.explanation_en: Both frequency words in this exchange take the habitual — अक्सर in the question and कभी-कभी in the answer — because both describe how often something happens rather than what is happening now. The second half switches to instructions, where धीरे is doing manner work rather than frequency. Notice तुम taking आते in the first line: plural agreement even for one person, as it has throughout.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Speak quietly, it is crowded here.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: All right, I will speak quietly.

common_error.wrong: तुम अक्सर यहाँ आ रहे हो?
common_error.why_en: अक्सर asks about frequency, which the continuous cannot express. The habitual is the only option.

practice.question: कभी-कभी आता हूँ
practice.explanation_en: कभी-कभी means sometimes, and it takes the habitual.

game.question_en: Listen to the first line. Which word is missing?
game.explanation_en: तुम takes plural agreement, so the participle is आते.

summary.recap_en: बिल्कुल strengthens whatever it touches and बिल्कुल नहीं is a flat refusal. सिर्फ़ must sit directly in front of what it limits, since its position decides the meaning exactly as only does in English.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the last of the adverbs, then the final verb block that closes the module.
